claims.text: Moderate alcohol intake of 5 to 14 g per day is associated with a decreased risk of coronary heart disease in middle-aged women.
Alcohol intake of 25 g or more per day is associated with a decreased risk of coronary heart disease in middle-aged women.
Moderate alcohol intake of 5 to 14 g per day is associated with a decreased risk of ischemic stroke in middle-aged women.
Alcohol intake of 5 to 14 g per day tends to be associated with an increased risk of subarachnoid hemorrhage in middle-aged women.

evidence.description: As compared with nondrinkers, women who consumed 5 to 14 g of alcohol per day had a relative risk of coronary disease of 0.6 (95 percent confidence interval, 0.4 to 0.9) after adjustment for risk factors.
For 25 g or more of alcohol per day the relative risk of coronary disease was 0.4 (95 percent confidence interval, 0.2 to 0.8) after adjustment for risk factors.
For 5 to 14 g of alcohol per day the relative risk of ischemic stroke was 0.3 (95 percent confidence interval, 0.1 to 0.7).
For 5 to 14 g of alcohol per day the relative risk of subarachnoid hemorrhage was 3.7 (95 percent confidence interval, 1.0 to 13.8).

methodologies.name: Prospective cohort study with dietary questionnaire assessment
methodologies.description: A prospective study following a female cohort to evaluate alcohol intake via questionnaire and track incident coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke, and subarachnoid hemorrhage.
conditions: 87,526 female nurses 34 to 59 years of age
Adjusted for coronary disease risk factors

limitations.text: The number of documented cases of subarachnoid hemorrhage was small (28 cases).
